hook.en: How does a company decide whether to open a new factory or rent one? It follows a definite sequence of steps called the *planning process*.

body.en: The steps are: setting objectives; developing premises (assumptions about the future); identifying alternative courses of action; evaluating alternative courses; selecting an alternative; implementing the plan; and follow-up action.

title.en: On the board: the planning process

narration.en: Watch the board as we build this up step by step.

say.en: Step one: set objectives. Everything else follows from them.
Step two: develop premises, the assumptions about the future.
Step three: identify alternative courses of action.
Step four: evaluate each alternative, for example by its profit.
Steps five and six: select the best alternative and implement it.
Step seven: follow up to see that the plan works.
Mnemonic: Some Doctors Iron Every Shirt In Fashion.

explanation.en: Objectives, premises, alternatives, evaluation, selection, implementation and follow-up.

steps.en: Set the objective: one new outlet earning a profit within a year
Develop premises: assume steady demand and rent in the area
Identify alternatives: a mall shop, a high-street shop or a kiosk
Evaluate each alternative's cost, risk and likely sales
Select the best alternative: the high-street shop
Implement the plan: lease, fit out, staff and open the shop
Follow up: check results and adjust the plan

problem.en: Expected sales are 12,000 units. Plan A: fixed cost ₹2,00,000, contribution ₹50 per unit. Plan B: fixed cost ₹5,00,000, contribution ₹80 per unit. Evaluate and select.

steps.en: Equal profit at (5,00,000 − 2,00,000) ÷ (80 − 50) = 10,000 units; sales of 12,000 exceed this.
Select Plan B, then implement it and follow up.

answer.en: Plan B, with ₹60,000 more profit at the expected sales of 12,000 units.

narration.en: Let us work through this case together. Expected sales are 12,000 units. Plan A: fixed cost ₹2,00,000, contribution ₹50 per unit. Plan B: fixed cost ₹5,00,000, contribution ₹80 per unit. Evaluate and select.

say.en: Let us work through this case together. Expected sales are 12,000 units. Plan A: fixed cost 2,00,000, rupees contribution 50 rupees per unit. Plan B: fixed cost 5,00,000, rupees contribution 80 rupees per unit. Evaluate and select.
Profit A equals 12,000 times 50 minus 2,00,000 equals 6,00,000 minus 2,00,000 equals 4,00,000 rupees.
Profit B equals 12,000 times 80 minus 5,00,000 equals 9,60,000 minus 5,00,000 equals 4,60,000 rupees.
Equal profit at (5,00,000 minus 2,00,000) divided by 80 minus 50 equals 10,000 units; sales of 12,000 exceed this.
Select Plan B, then implement it and follow up.
So the answer is Plan B, with 60,000 rupees more profit at the expected sales of 12,000 units.

Match the plans with their examples: i Objective ii Rule iii Budget iv Strategy, a "Increase market share to 25 percent in two years" b "Wear helmets on the shop floor" c "Sales of 5 rupees crore in the next quarter" d "Enter rural markets with low-priced packs to beat competition".
An objective is an end result, a rule allows no discretion, a budget is numerical, and a strategy is a comprehensive plan to reach objectives, considering competition.
